text:
Leah: :wave: Quick broadcast — we're rolling out a docs + SDK sample dependency policy change next week. TL;DR: samples and docs snippets will start enforcing pinned direct deps and reject unpinned transitive ranges. This is to prevent bitrot and surprising runtime breakages.

Leah: What this means for you: sample repos will receive automated PRs that pin transitive deps where safe, and docs snippets will include a small provenance footer with tested versions. We'll also add a CI gate in docs-ci that runs lightweight dependency checks.

Miguel: Any migration pain for teams using older SDK versions?

Leah: Good Q — we’re adding a compatibility shim in SDK v4.3 to tolerate pinned transitive deps for 6 months. If you're on v3.x, we'll publish a short upgrade patch + codemod.

Sam: Will the automated PRs be opt-in? Can we preview them? :eyes:

Leah: They'll be opt-out for main public samples (we want to keep examples healthy). But you can preview them — nightly canary runs will open PRs in a docs-sandbox org first. We’ll also post diffs in the preview channel.

Kate: Any change to snippet copy? We rely on quick copy/paste for users.

Leah: No functional change to snippets. We’ll append a single-line comment with the tested runtime toolchain, e.g., `# tested: python 3.10, sdk==4.2.1, deps pinned`. Copy/paste still works as-is.

Elliot: How about package managers? npm/Yarn/pnpm and pip?

Leah: Docs-ci will run both `pip check` and `npm ci && npm ls --parseable` for JS. The PRs will use the relevant lockfile (package-lock/pipfile-lock/poetry.lock).

docs-bot: Migration guide published: https://redwood.example.com/docs/migration/sample-deps-policy — includes codemod, opt-out instructions, and PR examples.

Miguel: Timeline?

Leah: Rollout timeline:
- 1735630000 (one week): canary runs + preview PRs in docs-sandbox.
- 1736360000 (≈1 month): auto-PRs to public sample repos (opt-out available).
- 1738150000 (≈3 months): docs-ci gate enforced for new snippet merges.

Sam: Who should we ping if the auto-PRs break local dev flows?

Leah: @Leah and @Elliot for immediate fixes; open issues with label `docs-migration` for tracking. We'll prioritize anything that blocks customer workflows.

Kate: Can we get a 30-min drop-in to walk through codemod and preview?

Leah: Yes — scheduled drop-in: 1735674000 (Zoom link in calendar invite). I’ll post slides and a short demo recording after the session.

Miguel: Thanks — appreciate the heads-up.

Leah: Thanks team — quick checklist for maintainers: 1) read migration guide, 2) watch preview PRs, 3) flag edge cases in `docs-migration`. Will follow up with a short FAQ. :sparkles: 

docs-bot: Action items created: `DOCS-3126` (codemod run), `DOCS-3127` (ci gate config), `DOCS-3128` (compatibility shim tests).

Elliot: Noted. If anyone wants a hand running the codemod locally I can pair up tomorrow.

Leah: Appreciate it — will coordinate pairing requests in DMs.
